title: TS-48 Disk dirty tracking and write guard (data-loss protection)
description:
Source: the re-audit report at /tmp/ts/reaudit.md plus the agent reports quoted here. Rules: features stay the spec (existing scenario text unchanged); cucumber-js steps drive production code; mutation check recorded per scenario group; no new Python; push with an explicit refspec.

From TS-47: three scenarios are tagged @needs-product-behavior and excluded in conversation/cucumber.mjs because no TypeScript sets diskDirty and nothing refuses a disk write before the intended host hydrates. They are real data-loss protection that Python had: computer_snapshots 'Unpublished live-disk writes block relocate' and 'The live disk cannot be written until the intended host hydrates', computer_snapshot_dynamo 'Unpublished writes mark disk dirty across a Dynamo recycle'. Also the two single_computer_start_disk_ownership scenarios (single live disk writer, wedged claim / write-lock clearing). Implement in the computer record and host protocol: a write or terminal action result marks the disk dirty until a snapshot publish; relocateComputer refuses while dirty (SnapshotRequiredError-style error); the host refuses writes before it has hydrated the snapshot the record names; the dirty flag round-trips through the Dynamo codec. Read how Python did it (git show origin/develop~N for the deleted Python domain code, or the pre-cutover python/src/chatticus) and mirror the behavior; where the design is silent (live-writer lock) decide minimally and record it in docs/TYPESCRIPT_CONTROL_PLANE.md. Then remove the tag, port the features' remaining scenarios to the manifest, and mutation-check each.
right_now_summary: The TypeScript re-audit is defining disk-dirty tracking and write guards before restoring excluded scenarios.
